speaker: Doctor
text: Please describe the characteristics of the blood in your urine, such as its color and whether you have seen any clots. Have you experienced fever, chills, nausea, or pain radiating to your groin?

speaker: Patient
text: 42-year-old Caucasian male. The patient reports experiencing visible blood in his urine accompanied by discomfort in his right flank. He denies any recent trauma to the area. He mentions a series of urinary tract infections over the past few years but has not been on renal dialysis.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for those details. To narrow down the cause, does the pain worsen with urination, and have you noticed any "streaks" of blood or distinct clots? REQUEST TEST: Urinalysis with microscopy and culture. REQUEST TEST: Serum creatinine and electrolytes.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Urinalysis: Appearance Reddish, WBC 10-20 /HPF, RBC Too numerous to count, Nitrites Negative, Leukocyte Esterase Positive. Serum Creatinine: 1.1 mg/dL.

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Hematuria and right flank pain. I also have History of recurrent urinary tract infections, No recent trauma.

speaker: Patient
text: Past medical history: No significant previous medical history except noted recurrent urinary tract infections. No history of renal dialysis or known genetic diseases. Social history: Non-smoker, drinks alcohol socially. Works in an office setting.

speaker: Patient
text: Denies fever, nausea, vomiting, diarrhea, dysuria, or any recent illnesses. To keep my notes clear, please give only one final answer and keep it to a single direct conclusion.

speaker: Doctor
text: Based on the hematuria and flank pain without dysuria or fever, I need to evaluate for urolithiasis or malignancy. REQUEST TEST: Renal ultrasound and Non-contrast CT KUB. REQUEST IMAGES.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Intravenous Pyelogram Findings: Multiple cysts present in the collecting ducts of the medulla. No obstruction noted.
